I recently bought a .40 for home defense and the range. I thought it would make a great defensive weapon as the rounds are bigger than a 9mm. I like the gun but people have been giving me shit for it.

Why all the hate?
What are your thoughts on .40 S&W hand guns?

A .40 S&W is more similar to a 9mm than a 45acp. As /u/bob3333 said, the .40 was based off of the 10mm in order to make a more manageable round. The 10mm kicks and preforms similar to the 45acp while the .40 kicks and preforms closer to the 9mm.

Here's some good reading material/data on the rounds. 9mm .40 10mm .45

I love mine... let me explain:

Everyone here has gone over the disadvantages of the 40S&W -- less capacity, nearly identical ballistics as the 9mm, more snappy than the 9mm -- but who cares?

Sure, you get less capacity than a similar handgun in 9mm, but that is usually one round per magazine. It's not like you're losing dozens of rounds per mag, which would make a huge difference, it's just one (maybe two) round(s). That's not enough to make me hate an entire ammo caliber.

Yes, the ballistics are SIMILAR to the 9mm, but they are NOT the same. Due to the higher speeds and higher mass, the 40S&W will achieve deeper, more consistent penetration than a regular 9mm -- not counting +P or +P+ loads since not all pistols can handle those, but all 40S&W pistols can handle all 40S&W loads.

And that last point brings a snappier round, but if anyone tells you that this is a reason to ditch a gun, then they're not a gun owner. All gun owners know that you practice with what you have, and get good at it. Not all of us can afford a Browning, so we practice with our Remingtons, and we get good at it... Not all of us can afford an H&K, so we practice with whatever we have, and we get good at it... In no way is the snap, from a 40, unmanageable to the point that you can't practice with it and get good at shooting it -- unless you have a medical disorder and can't hold onto the weapon.

Now that we've gone over the cons, let's go over the pros that I've found:

All of the police (state, local, and highway) in my area carry 40S&W, EXCLUSIVELY. This means that, if I every need more ammo, especially in a SHTF situation, I can make up for that one (or two) missing round(s) by getting them from literally anywhere. The feds also carry 40S&W, but I hear that they're moving to 9mm... but that has yet to happen.

Because the 40S&W has different ballistics, self-defense (SD) ammo has better expansion rates than 9mm, reducing the chance of a pass-through -- depending on the ammo type. From my personal research (which mimics tnoutdoors9), more 9mm SD loads fail more often than 40S&W loads. Sure, both can fail, and pass-thruogh, but it tends to happen more often in 9mm... especially in +P and +P+ loads.

My first handgun was a 40S&W, because my brother had a 9mm and we wanted to compare the two, which is not to say that I don't own a metric fuck-ton of 9mm pistols... So, I bought range ammo and SD ammo in 40, and gathered a stockpile... again, not to say I don't have a stockpile in 9mm, but the 40S&W has had more time, and is larger. This has fed into the "machine," causing me to buy more 40-pistols, feeding back into the machine making me buy more 40-ammo. So, even though I have a "stockpile" of all calibers I own, nothing compares to the 40S&W area.

Also, that practice thing is a HUGE ticket item: Because I have so much/many 40S&W items, I practice with it almost exclusively. I'll take my AR to the range, and shoot my SD pistol (in 40) while I'm there, for practice. I'll go to shoot some skeet, and pull out my SD pistol, for practice. I'll go to the archery range, and practice with my SD while I'm out there. So I have the most trigger time with the 40S&W, and I'm the most comfortable with it. The "snappiness" is there, but I don't "notice" it anymore, and I shoot better in 40 than I do in 9.

In short, don't let anyone tell you that your caliber choice is bad. You shoot whatever you're comfortable with shooting, and you practice with it. If you can only shoot a 22LR, and that's what you carry, don't let anyone give you any shit... you can't miss enough to stop a bad guy. If you don't "trust" anything smaller than a 50MAG, then that's up to you and don't let anyone dissuade you from carrying what you're comfortable shooting... just get plenty of practice.

Also, it's good to have a wide "range" of calibers, as per my first pro bullet point. Sure, more people tend to like the 9mm, but 40S&W is EVERYWHERE, and if you limit yourself to ONLY 9mm handguns, when that dries up, what are you going to do? It's like when we had that ammo "crisis" a year, or two, ago: I was able to go to the range every week, since I had weapons in every caliber, and I could shoot all of the calibers that were currently available... no 9mm in stock: I'll shoot 40S&W... no 40S&W in stock: I'll shoot 45ACP... no 45ACP in stock: I'll shoot .380... no .380 in stock: I'll shoot 5.7. Diversity is key, here.

There is nothing immediately damning about the 40S&W to make you avoid it like the plague. Just shoot what you like, and let all the haters stew in their pools of "superiority."
